name: Luiss Guido Carli
summary: Private university in Rome for business, economics, law and politics; five English bachelor's, with a direct offer for IB students on 36 points.

ib.text: IB Diploma or predicted grades of 36/45 or more give direct admission (EU/Schengen route). Below that, sit the online Luiss Test (SAT-style: logic, problem-solving, maths).

programmes.name: Business Administration
programmes.about: Business economics with management, finance, law, quantitative methods and IT, taught in English with an international, multidisciplinary outlook.
programmes.overview: The first two years build the base: microeconomics, accounting, calculus, corporate law, management theory, statistics and macroeconomics, then marketing, financial analysis, EU law and corporate finance, with coding labs and specialised software training. Learning is project-based, including a Grand Challenge practical component and an internship or company project. In the third year you choose a major in Marketing, Organizational Behavior and HR, or International Business and Strategy. International options include the ACE triple degree with Renmin University and George Washington University, Erasmus+ and free-mover semesters. Graduates go into multinationals, start-ups, consulting, financial institutions and marketing management.
programmes.selectionNote: Direct offer with IB 36/45 (predicted counts), SAT 1200 or ACT 25; otherwise you sit the online Luiss Test in English.

programmes.name: Economics and Business
programmes.about: Economics, management, finance, law and quantitative methods, with particular attention to European institutions, market regulation, competition and antitrust.
programmes.overview: A shared two-year foundation covers micro and macroeconomics, international economics, mathematics, statistics and applied econometrics, business economics, accounting, corporate finance, law, and data analysis and coding. In the third year you pick a major: Management, Finance, or Economics, which looks at growth, development, inequality, public policy and competition. Teaching mixes lectures, workshops, project work, simulations and real-world cases. Exchange options include the EU-TriBE triple degree with Universite libre de Bruxelles and Goethe University Frankfurt, Erasmus+ and free-mover semesters. Graduates go into consulting, finance, strategy and international organisations, or on to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: Direct offer with IB 36/45 (predicted counts), SAT 1200 or ACT 25; otherwise you sit the online Luiss Test in English.

programmes.name: Global Law
programmes.about: Law for cross-border careers in multinationals, NGOs and European and international organisations, with economics, management and tech, focused on global governance and human rights.
programmes.overview: Years one and two give every student a shared grounding in constitutional, private, EU, administrative, international, comparative and criminal law. In year three you choose Global Law, Business and Tech, which looks at law and technology and financial markets, Global Law and International Organizations, or an Italian Law track with a fast route to a single-cycle master's. Teaching goes beyond lectures to workshops, project work, simulations, legal clinics and the Grand Challenge. Exchanges and summer schools are available. Graduates work in European and international institutions, NGOs and multinationals, in compliance and institutional relations, or go on to a master's in law or international relations.
programmes.selectionNote: Direct offer with IB 36/45 (predicted counts), SAT 1200 or ACT 25; otherwise you sit the online Luiss Test in English.

programmes.name: Management and Artificial Intelligence
programmes.about: Management and economics combined with quantitative and IT skills, to apply AI, big data and machine learning to business decisions and strategy.
programmes.overview: Year one covers mathematics, programming, microeconomics, algorithms, digital business management and statistical modelling, with labs on real challenges from industry or academia. Year two moves to machine learning, organisational data integration and social network analysis, anchored by the Grand Challenge, where groups apply data analysis and AI to real business problems. In year three you study databases, financial technologies and AI regulation, with electives, an internship and a final thesis. No prior IT knowledge is needed. A double degree exists with Kozminski University. Graduates work in data analysis, AI strategy and digital transformation, or continue to master's programmes in data science and AI.
programmes.selectionNote: Direct offer with IB 36/45 (predicted counts), SAT 1200 or ACT 25; otherwise you sit the online Luiss Test in English.

programmes.name: Politics: Philosophy and Economics
programmes.about: Philosophy, politics and economics with law, history, sociology and quantitative methods; a third-year track in AI, sustainability or fundamental rights.
programmes.overview: The first year covers microeconomics, contemporary history, sociology, political philosophy, public law, statistics and mathematical analysis, plus an AI literacy and coding lab; the second adds macroeconomics, international relations, political science, the history of political thought, social research methods and EU and international law. In year three you pick a concentration in Artificial Intelligence, Sustainability or Fundamental Rights. Teaching includes data analysis workshops, seminars, internships and study abroad, with double degrees with Victoria University of Wellington and Sciences Po Bordeaux. Graduates move into international organisations, government, think tanks, NGOs and companies, or on to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: Direct offer with IB 36/45 (predicted counts), SAT 1200 or ACT 25; otherwise you sit the online Luiss Test in English.

notes: The full 2027-28 admission notice comes out from October 2026, when applications open; each route costs €150 to enter.
The degree you choose when you apply is binding for admission and enrolment.
Luiss also runs a second Luiss Test session for EU students; its dates were not yet published.
